still_wrong.title: A new formula still freezes the page for 4 to 6 s on its first Landscape
still_wrong.detail:
Fresh formulas, loaded on the 2D view, then __cmwSetMain('land'), base and this build alternating. The longest main-thread gap (rAF):
- This build: 9 of 11 runs stall 3.4 to 6.3 s. Examples: sqrt(z^5-2z) cosh(z/5) 5.96 s, log(z^5+6) cos(z/7) 3.73 s, sqrt(z^4+z+5) sinh(z/7) 4.47 s, tanh(z^3/4)+sqrt(z-2) 4.74 s.
- A formula with no cut stalls as long (z^3/(cosh z+8) 6.27 s, z^4/(sinh z+13) 5.03 s), and it has no edge pass (cuts 0). So the edge program is not the cause, or not the only one.
- Base: 11 of 11 runs have no gap over 0.75 s.
- The surface is first on screen 4.6 to 7.3 s after the switch on this build, against 0.4 to 1.1 s on base.
- With All sheets on, there is no stall (0.39 to 0.51 s, base 0.62 s).
The likely cause is the principal land program's compile. LAND_FS now calls the chain about six times for the wall lookup (landW at vZ, at both bracket ends, in the false-position loop and twice at zs). Not confirmed per program (time box).
The ledger's cold-start numbers ('first surface 0.15 to 1.04 s') come from a flawed probe. coldstart_cmd.js stamps a frame's time before Page.captureScreenshot, and the capture itself blocks through the stall. So a frame stamped at about 0.2 s is the picture from after the freeze.
still_wrong.evidence: review-verify/cs1.js, cs2.js, cs3.js (outputs quoted above). cs2 and cs3 also record when each capture returns. Example: sqrt(z^5-2z) cosh(z/5) drawn in the capture started at 255 ms that returned at 7261 ms, with gaps [229 ms: 786 ms] and [1262 ms: 5961 ms].
still_wrong.fix:
Find which program blocks: log getProgramParameter(LINK_STATUS) and first-draw times per program. If it is LAND_FS:
- Do not let the wall lookup gate the first frame. Compile the principal land shader with uWallFit's code behind a separate program, the plain one first, and swap when it is ready (KHR_parallel_shader_compile, as the edge pass now does).
- Or keep one landW call site: put the bracket ends, the loop and the final zs evaluation in one loop with a uniform trip count.
Re-measure with the capture's end time, and gate on base + 0.3 s to first surface and no main-thread gap over base + 100 ms.

still_wrong.title: Pole walls are now a broken, speckled band; speckles also show on the user's walls
still_wrong.detail:
The main wall faces are smooth now. The user's walls at t = 0.2 have no fluting or colour stripes, and the contours run straight and level (pictures-3 holds there). But where the wall lookup falls back, the fix leaves a new artifact that is worse than a pleat:
- tan z Re: at every pole a vertical band of dashed dark scratches and pixel noise crosses the wall. It is visible at 1:1, light and dark.
- sec z Re (dark): the same noisy seam where the purple wall meets the green one.
- The user's sin sqrt z at t = 0.2, All sheets, Im: salt-and-pepper dots in a narrow vertical strip on the teal wall, next to the grey slab, and on the pink wall behind. Light and dark.
The ledger calls this 'slightly broken'. In pictures it reads as noise, not as a surface, which is not article-grade.
still_wrong.evidence: review-verify/crop-tan-sec-pole-band-4x.png (left: tan Re light; right: sec Re dark), crop-user-t0.2-wall-speckle-4x.png (light | dark), full frames p-tan-re-light.png, p-sec-re-dark.png, p-user-t0.2-im-sh-{light,dark}.png.
still_wrong.fix: Where the lookup falls back (keep < 1, or no bracket), do not mix per pixel between zs and vZ. The choice flips between neighbouring pixels, and dFdx/dFdy of zs then blow up, which gives both the dots and the scratches. Make the fallback continuous: fade the tiles and contours by the error alone and use the facet's own normal. Or clamp gT and the zs derivatives, and choose the root nearest the previous one along the level line. The root fix is still design 3.3.
